concepts.hy: Health, gingivitis and extent use related but distinct bleeding thresholds.
Smoking can mute visible inflammation while increasing periodontitis risk.
The ADA/FDA selection guide relies on clinical judgment and sets no recall interval.
Stage uses the worst site, tooth loss and complexity factors.
Use longitudinal evidence first, then indirect evidence and smoking or diabetes modifiers.
Abscess and necrotizing disease have distinct acute clinical patterns.
Baseline comparison and bone changes separate implant health, mucositis and peri-implantitis.
Tooth and patient factors both shape a prognosis that can change.
Reevaluation determines whether residual pockets need step 3 or supportive care.
Supportive care intervals are individualized within a 3- to 12-month range.

box.cc: "My gums bleed when I brush." (6 months)
hx: Type 2 diabetes; recent HbA1c 6.8%
Smokes 5 cigarettes per day
Four teeth were removed for orthodontic treatment; no teeth were lost to periodontitis
No comparable periodontal charts or images from the prior five years; no medication allergies
findings: Tooth 3 mesiobuccal: PD 6 mm, interdental CAL 5 mm, BOP present, RBL 35% reaching the middle third on a 2D radiograph
Tooth 14 distal: PD 5 mm, CAL 4 mm, BOP present, RBL 18%
Eight of 28 present teeth are involved; 28 teeth remain
No vertical bone loss of 3 mm or more, no Class II or III furcation, no moderate ridge defect, stable bite, no mobility degree 2 or greater
No prior five-year progression measurement is available

box.cc: "My gums bleed and several teeth feel loose." (4 months)
hx: Type 2 diabetes; recent HbA1c 7.2%
Smokes 12 cigarettes per day
Five teeth have been lost to periodontitis; 17 teeth remain
No comparable periodontal chart or radiograph from the prior five years
findings: Tooth 14 mesiobuccal: PD 7 mm, interdental CAL 6 mm, BOP present, RBL 46% reaching the middle third
Vertical bone loss 3 mm; Class II furcation involvement; moderate ridge defect
Bite is stable; no complex rehabilitation need or mobility degree 2 or greater documented
Thirteen of 17 present teeth show periodontitis involvement

box.cc: "The gum by this molar is very sore." (2 days)
hx: Periodontitis is recorded in the dental history
No medication allergies; no current fever
findings: Tooth 19 has an established periodontal pocket with localized purulent drainage from the gingival wall
Tooth 19 furcation: 4 mm horizontal attachment loss without through-and-through passage; vertical subclass depth 5 mm from the fornix

box.cc: "My gums bleed when I brush." (2 weeks)
hx: No history of periodontitis, recession treatment or crown lengthening
Does not smoke; no medications or known allergies
findings: Plaque and supragingival calculus are present
BOP at 22% of sites; all probing depths are 3 mm or less
No attachment loss or radiographic bone loss

box.cc: "One area still feels deep after the cleaning visits." (3 weeks)
hx: Stage III periodontitis; completed step 1 and step 2 therapy
Reports consistent home care and attends follow-up appointments
No medication allergies
findings: Tooth 30 has a residual pocket measuring 6 mm after subgingival instrumentation
Tooth 30 is a mandibular molar; furcation examination shows 4 mm horizontal loss without through-and-through passage and a 5 mm vertical subclass depth
No other pocket of 6 mm or more; plaque control has been maintained

items.stem: Three months after regenerative surgery, reevaluation finds no bleeding pocket deeper than 4 mm and no pocket measuring 6 mm or more.

box.cc: "The implant area bleeds when I clean it." (1 month)
hx: History of stage III periodontitis; currently in supportive care
Smokes 3 cigarettes per day
Implant prosthesis completed three years ago; baseline probing and radiograph were recorded then
findings: Implant at site 19: bleeding on gentle probing, probing depth increased from 4 mm at baseline to 7 mm, bone level is 3 mm more apical than on the baseline radiograph
Implant at site 30: no bleeding or suppuration, no depth increase, and no bone loss beyond initial remodeling
Tooth 3: PD 5 mm, CAL 4 mm, Class II furcation involvement

box.cc: "I am here for my maintenance visit." (scheduled visit)
hx: Successfully treated periodontitis; completed steps 1 and 2
Type 2 diabetes; recent HbA1c 8.1%
Smokes 12 cigarettes per day
Reports taking medicines as prescribed and attends supportive care
findings: All probing depths are 4 mm or less; no 4 mm site bleeds; BOP at 6% of sites
Plaque is visible at several sites; no deep residual pocket is recorded
The patient asks whether an adjunct medicine should be added to maintenance care

box.cc: "The gum around this tooth suddenly became painful." (1 day)
hx: Stage III periodontitis; completed step 1 and step 2
Plaque control has been maintained
No known medication allergies
findings: A pre-existing pocket at tooth 3, a maxillary molar has localized pus in the gingival wall and rapid tissue change
Residual pocket at tooth 3 measures 6 mm after the acute lesion has been controlled
Class II furcation involvement is present at the buccal and mesial sites of tooth 3
The patient reports reliable home care; no other pocket of 6 mm or more

box.cc: "The gum looks enlarged and one tooth has receded." (6 months)
hx: Takes phenytoin for seizure prevention
Tooth 8 has been evaluated for pulpal-periodontal communication
No known medication allergies
findings: Tooth 8 has a vertical root fracture and a pathologic communication between pulpal and periodontal tissues
At tooth 10, buccal recession is 3 mm and interproximal attachment loss is 2 mm
CEJ is detectable; cervical step is 0.6 mm; gingival thickness and keratinized-tissue width are recorded
Firm gingival enlargement of the anterior papillae, more than the plaque level would explain
